x: Dick Negus is with an officers' training unit in Kent. He injured a knee on an assault course and is to have an operation.

Dick Negus and Boxall of the Juniors and Leigh have possibilities, but need to do a lot of study of technique to show their best. The Hop, Step and Jump, rather a neglected event heretofore, we have tried to popularise by including the event in matches.
Alan Sexton and Dick Negus give promise of better performances to come, while Arthur Bruce was outstanding over the middle-distance races in our Junior matches.
The field events saw the Police gaining most points, but Sid Jones, now out of the Army, showed some of his old form in the Shot Putt, and young Dick Negus won the High Jump.
In the Junior match the Cambridge boys won both sprint races with Dick Negus and G.

Held on the same evening as the Inter-Club Walking contest at Tooting, The Club had two field event handicaps open to members. Dick Negus won the High Jump, and also did the best scratch jump, while B.

Arthur Bruce won the 1 Mile, followed by Eddie Short and Len Bishop, and this trio are certainly "hot stuff" in Junior team races. Dick Negus won the Long Jump and the total points were: Cambridge H. 16, Belgrave H. 13.

Dick Negus made a good start by winning the 100 Yards, although Sexton of the School was only beaten by inches. The latter showed good form in winning the 220 Yards, and has now joined the Club, a must useful addition to our ranks.

… Junior matches to be held, owing to the number of competitors being limited, it was decided to merge the two contests. Dick Negus ran well in the Junior 100, while Dicky Dumbrill took second place in the Senior event, and also won the 220 Yards race.…
Dick Negus and Alan Sexton were also running at another meeting, and it seems that we shall have to make certain of having our strongest team out when next we meet this school.
It was a very closely contested match and the result was decided on the result of the Relay race. Alan Sexton, now running for his school, beat Dick Negus in the 100, and also won the 220 Yards.
Dick Negus won the final, beating Alan Sexton with A.

Held at Tooting on July 17th, this proved a very closely fought match between the home club, the Polytechnic Juniors, and our lads. Dick Negus ran well to gain third place in the 100, while G. Osmint also did well in finishing second in the 220 Yards.
Dick Negus was off form in the jumping events and is maybe feeling the effects of a very full season. Final match points were : Belgrave H. 75, Metropolitan Police 46.

Basil Walden, a past Surrey junior sprint champion, beat Dick Negus with Alan Sexton third, in a very closely contested final. We also had two heats in the Club 220 Yards Championship, and the final was between Botwright, Machell, Read and Dumbrill.

In the Junior contest, Dick Negus was second in his heat of the 80 Yards Sprint, and then in the 1 Mile Team race. Arthur Bruce was third in the individual race and was well backed up by Eddie Short, but Len Bishop found the pace too hot and was some way behind.
With only one representative allowed from each team, we had the individual winner in every event, bar one. Dick Negus won the 100 Yards and also the High and Long Jumps.

Bruty, of S.L.H., won both sprint races and Dick Negus was second in the 100 and Alan Sexton was second in the 220. Betterton and Freestone were first and second in the 440 and Eric Bishop gained third place in the 880 Yards.
The final was a closely-contested race between three of our junior members, and Alan Sexton just beat Dick Negus, with D.

Dick Negus was one of our members who travelled over, as did Charlie Jones, and Dick won the 100 yards, and was also second in the High Jump, and then capped a busy afternoon's work by winning the 220.
Dick Negus has again been our best High Jumper. His best performance of 5 feet 7 inches was achieved with the new “ Straddle ” style, which he seems to be mastering.

With Dick Negus back in training, and, we hope, back to his form of two years ago, we should be quite strong in this event. We hope also to have the assistance of John Boxall now that his examinations are nearly at an end.
